regulator: New York Office of Cannabis Management

data_source.name: OCM Cannabis Control Board meeting presentations (monthly sales charts) and OCM's Metrc 'Cannabis Market Landscape' dashboard
data_source.notes: New York has no downloadable monthly sales file. Monthly rows are read from official charts: January 2023-November 2025 are adult-use sales self-reported by retailers, from the December 18, 2025 Cannabis Control Board deck (OCM rounds to $0.1 million; some months are marked with an asterisk in OCM's chart, with no legend on the slide). From January 2026 OCM moved to Metrc data: monthly totals (adult-use and medical combined) are the exact figures shown in OCM's Metrc-hosted Cannabis Market Landscape dashboard, and the adult-use/medical split is from OCM's July 2 and October 1, 2026 board presentations, so the split may not add exactly to the total. December 2025 is missing because no official source shows a full-month total. The break between self-reported adult-use data (to 2025) and Metrc adult-use plus medical data (2026) means the two periods are not strictly comparable. Annual figures are from the OCM 2025 Annual Report, Table 8 (2025 covers January-November).

tax_note: Adult-use retail sales carry a 9% state and 4% local retail excise tax (13% in all), plus a 9% distributor tax at wholesale; adult-use cannabis is not subject to regular sales tax (NYS Department of Taxation and Finance).
summary: New York's legal adult-use market opened in December 2022 and grew slowly at first because licensing was tied up in litigation, then accelerated sharply as hundreds of stores opened in 2024 and 2025. Adult-use sales rose from $155 million in 2023 to $882 million in 2024 and $1.48 billion in the first 11 months of 2025, per the Office of Cannabis Management. State officials reported $1.41 billion in retail sales in the first three quarters of 2026 and more than $4.1 billion since launch. New York City accounts for the largest share. Medical sales keep shrinking as patients move to adult-use stores.

faq.q: How much cannabis does New York sell?
faq.a: Adult-use sales were $1.48 billion in January-November 2025, and state officials reported $1.41 billion in retail sales for the first three quarters of 2026.

faq.q: Does New York publish monthly cannabis sales?
faq.a: Not as a downloadable file. The OCM shows monthly sales as charts in its Cannabis Control Board presentations and in its Metrc-hosted Cannabis Market Landscape dashboard; this page records those figures, for example $174.4 million in October 2026 (adult-use and medical combined).

faq.q: How much is the cannabis tax in New York?
faq.a: Shoppers pay a 13% retail excise (9% state, 4% local); distributors also pay a 9% tax at wholesale. Regular sales tax does not apply.
